reason: The compute-resources FAQ answer states memory choice with proportional CPU, and the 256MB vs 128MB / 512MB example exactly as claimed.
Quote under the compute-resources question states memory can be set from 128MB to 10,240MB, matching both values.
Under the Lambda MicroVMs section the quote says MicroVMs support up to 32 GB of memory and 16 vCPUs; scope and 'up to' match.
SLA question answer states coverage by the Lambda SLA with at least 99.5% Monthly Uptime Percentage for instance-level availability.
Suspend-and-resume answer states memory and disk state preserved for up to 8 hours with no compute charge while suspended.
The 'What is AWS Lambda MicroVMs?' answer states every part of the claim nearly verbatim.
Monitoring answer lists the same real-time CloudWatch metrics as the claim.
Answer to the limit question is 'No' plus a default safety throttle per account per region; context adds the Service Quotas increase, so adjustable holds.
Charging answer states Lambda is priced on a pay-per-use basis.
Under 'When should I use Provisioned Concurrency?' the quote says concurrency can be increased, lowered or turned off completely.
Quote says Application Auto Scaling can configure schedules or adjust Provisioned Concurrency in real time as demand changes.
Pricing answer states payment for configured concurrency and its period, plus Requests and Duration when the function executes.
Quote states Provisioned Concurrency keeps functions initialized and ready to respond in double-digit milliseconds.
Quote names the same latency-sensitive use cases (web or mobile backends, synchronous APIs, interactive microservices).
Quote says per-function maximum concurrent executions can reserve account concurrency for critical functions or cap downstream traffic.
Under the DynamoDB/Kinesis polling question the quote says the function role determines which resources Lambda can poll.
Event-source answer states CloudTrail and others act as event sources by logging to S3 and using S3 bucket notifications.
Quote says a resource policy rule granting access is created, but does not say it is created on the function; the claim adds that location.
Quote states the concurrency scaling limit is function-level and each function scales independently.
Quote states each synchronously invoked function can scale up to 1000 concurrent executions every 10 seconds; condition kept.
Quote recommends client-side KMS encryption, ciphertext in the environment variable, and decrypt logic in function code.
Quote describes snapshotting initialized memory and disk state, caching it, and resuming from the pre-initialized snapshot.
Claim repeats the quote under the SnapStart charges question verbatim, including the up to 14 days cache limit.
Quote says SnapStart and PC cannot be enabled at the same time on the same function.
Quote states caching charge while the version is active (minimum 3 hours, then per millisecond) and a restore charge, both memory-dependent.
Quote lists Java 11 and newer, Python 3.12 and newer, .NET 8 and newer; the claim does not say 'only'.
Claim matches the quote verbatim: from several seconds to as low as sub-second.
Quote says a SnapStart function can be configured to access resources in a VPC.
Quote says SnapStart is best-effort, does not guarantee eliminating cold starts, and recommends PC for strict double-digit millisecond startup.
Quote says function role or queue resource policy, and the more restrictive applies when both are present.
Quote states the stateless model, scaling to as many copies as needed, and access to stateful data through S3 or DynamoDB.
Quote states retry until success or data expiry and retention of a minimum of 24 hours for Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams.
Quote says S3-invoked events rejected by Lambda may be retained and retried by S3 for 24 hours; 'may' is kept.
Quote says synchronous invocations return a throttling error (429 error code) when the concurrency limit is exceeded.
Quote states up to 15 minutes per execution and a timeout between 1 second and 15 minutes.
Read with its heading on remaining available during updates, the 'Yes' answer gives the brief window, typically under a minute, of old or new version.
Quote says by default each function has a single current version and clients can call a specific version or the latest.
Quote says dual-stack VPC communication is over IPv4 by default and can be configured for IPv6.
Quote says VPC-configured functions do not have internet access as a default configuration; context gives the way to change it.
Quote says VPC access is enabled by specifying subnet and security group in the function configuration.
